newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul shares post selective gains.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul shares post selective gains.

text.p: Istanbul's stock market index rose on highly selective purchases on Wednesday following a four-day holiday, brokers said.

But majority of the shares, 122 out of 227 traded, fell, 81 rose and 24 were unchanged. The IMKB-100 closed at 83,692.58, up 1,271.6 points, or 1.54 percent from Friday. The market was closed on Monday and Tuesday due to Republic day.
Trade volume surged to 20.65 trillion lira ($215 million) from Friday's 12.84 trillion ($134 million).
Brokers said bluechip flat steel firm Eregli, was among the top earners with a 14.3 percent jump from Friday and was a major factor behind the index's rise due to its high market capitalisation.
Eregli and three utilities were the top four active shares which together made up 41.1 percent of the total turnover.
"The market became highly selective with players mostly switching shares depending on companies' nine-month profits," said Resat Kutucular from Toros securities.

"Technically, the index is at a critical level from where it can move either way. Sentiment looks good, but there is no substantial reason to back a rally. So if the index slips below 81,000, it may fall towards 75,000," Kutucular said.
Some brokers expect range-bound trade between 81,000 and 84,000 unless fresh cash inflow increases.
The index had surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to last Wednesday's all-time high close of 83,772.33, the tenth record in the medium-term uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level.
